# Water at forty

The pool tile was pale and cold. I stood on the deck with a wristband and no fear left.
Breath came fast. Legs did the math. Arms opened wider than pride could allow.
A lifeguard nodded. A kid paddled past. I tried to be lighter than panic.
The first inch was the worst. Then the pull of my hands turned my body into a small boat.
Back and front. Kick and breathe. The water closed over my ears and then let me go.
By the end of the hour my body knew a rhythm. It did not praise me or shame me. It simply carried.

More soon.
